status: drafted via multi-agent workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text, adversarially fact-checked and corrected
notes: Read in full from Assets/Resources/Verses/Ethiopian/1_samuel_9.json (all 31 chapters, 810 verses). This Ethiopian-translation text of 1 Samuel is, verse for verse, word-for-word identical to the standard KJV text of 1 Samuel — no structural, canonical, or content differences were found (unlike some other Ethiopian-canon books, e.g. this Bible's own 9-chapter 'Ezra' following the 1 Esdras tradition). Every event, name, speech, and chapter division checked against the real extracted text matches the already-completed KJV CharacterIndex for this book exactly: Hannah's vow and Samuel's birth (ch.1-2), Eli's house and its judgment (ch.2-4), the Ark's capture/plagues-among-the-Philistines/return (ch.4-7), Israel's demand for a king and Samuel's warning of 'the manner of the king' (ch.8), Saul's rise, rejection, and death (ch.9-15, 28, 31), David's anointing, rise, flight, and exploits (ch.16-27, 29-30). One cosmetic extraction artifact noted, not a content difference: 21:1 has a stray double space ('and  Ahimelech') from the source file, not a textual variant. Because the underlying text is identical to KJV, this draft mirrors the validated KJV 1Samuel.json's tier/character structure closely by design (same events genuinely warrant the same tiers), but every id is suffixed '_ethiopian' to keep this translation's character index fully independent per the schema's collision rule, and every verse note below was re-written directly from this translation's own extracted text rather than copied from the KJV file. Naming collisions carried forward and re-verified directly against this text: three distinct men named Abinadab (of Kirjath-jearim, 7:1; Jesse's son, 17:13; Saul's son, 31:2); two women named Ahinoam (Saul's wife, 14:50; David's wife, 25:43); two named Ahimelech (the priest of Nob, ch.21-22; 'Ahimelech the Hittite,' one of David's men, 26:6); two named Phinehas within the wider canon (Eli's son here versus Aaron's grandson elsewhere, not this book); Ahitub of 14:3/22:9,20 traced to 'the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli,' making Ahimelech and Abiathar descendants of Eli's line, consistent with the KJV finding. 1 Samuel 13:1's reign-length numeral reads incomplete in this text as well ('Saul reigned one year; and when he had reigned two years over Israel') — flagged as the same recognized textual crux, no invented age supplied.

children: three unnamed sons and two unnamed daughters born after Samuel, 2:21

verses.note: One of Elkanah's two wives; 'had no children,' set against the fruitful Peninnah.
Prays in bitterness of soul at Shiloh and vows that if given a son she will 'give him unto the LORD all the days of his life,' and no razor will touch his head.
Conceives and bears Samuel, naming him for having 'asked him of the LORD.'
Weans Samuel and brings him to Eli at Shiloh, lending him to the LORD 'as long as he liveth.'
Prays/sings a song exalting the LORD who raises the poor and beggar and brings down the proud — thematically anticipates the reversal of Eli's house for Samuel's, and of Saul's for David's.
Brings Samuel a coat yearly; the LORD 'visited Hannah' afterward with three more sons and two daughters.

characters.name: Elkanah
characters.perkNote: Gives Hannah 'a worthy portion' out of love despite her barrenness (1:5) and defers to her wish to keep Samuel home until weaned.

verses.note: Gives Peninnah and her children portions, but gives Hannah a worthy portion, 'for he loved Hannah.'
Comforts grieving Hannah: 'am not I better to thee than ten sons?'
Agrees to Hannah's plan to keep Samuel until weaned: 'do what seemeth thee good.'

characters.name: Peninnah
characters.perkNote: Her yearly provocation of Hannah (1:6-7) is the friction that drives Hannah to the temple and her vow, indirectly setting the book's opening chain of events in motion.

verses.note: Elkanah's other wife, who has children; provokes Hannah 'sore, for to make her fret,' year by year.

characters.name: Eli

verses.note: Priest at Shiloh seated by the temple post; mistakes silently-praying Hannah for drunk, then blesses her petition once corrected.
Hears of his sons' abuses and lying with women at the tabernacle door; rebukes them verbally but does not restrain them; the text notes they did not heed him, 'because the LORD would slay them.'
An unnamed man of God pronounces judgment on his house for honoring his sons above the LORD, foretelling both sons dead in one day and the priesthood passing elsewhere.
Young Samuel relays the LORD's confirming judgment; Eli answers, 'it is the LORD: let him do what seemeth him good.'

Waits anxiously by the wayside for battle news; on hearing the Ark is taken and both sons dead, falls backward off his seat and dies of a broken neck, being old and heavy; had judged Israel forty years.

funFacts: Eli's death by the gate closes the era of the judges just as Samuel's rise opens the transition toward kingship.

ageEvents.event: Dies of a broken neck falling from his seat on hearing the Ark was taken and both sons dead

characters.name: Hophni
characters.perkNote: The corrupt sacrificial-portion abuse (2:12-17) is described jointly for 'the sons of Eli,' not individually attributed to Hophni; he is differentiated only by being named first and dying alongside Phinehas carrying the Ark.

verses.note: Named with Phinehas as 'sons of Belial' who forcibly took meat with a fleshhook before the fat was burnt, threatening any priest's servant who resisted — a shared practice, not individually differentiated.
Carries the Ark to the battle line at Aphek; dies alongside Phinehas the day it is captured, fulfilling the earlier prophecy.

characters.name: Phinehas (son of Eli)
characters.perkNote: Shares Hophni's collective sin (2:12-17) but is individually distinguished by the aftermath of his own death — his wife's labor, collapse, and naming of Ichabod are tied specifically to him (4:19-22).

spouses: unnamed, dies in childbirth on hearing of his death and the Ark's capture, 4:19-20
genealogy.note: NAMING COLLISION: this Phinehas, son of Eli, is a different person from the far more prominent Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron elsewhere in the canon — not this book.

verses.note: Shares the corrupt sacrificial-portion practice jointly with Hophni; the text does not distinguish either brother's individual conduct.
Carries the Ark to battle; dies the same day it is captured.
His pregnant, unnamed wife goes into labor on hearing of the Ark's capture and her husband's and father-in-law's deaths; dies in childbirth, naming her son 'the glory is departed from Israel.'
Later referenced as father of Ahitub, the genealogical link this index uses (with 22:9,20) tracing Ahimelech and Abiathar back to Eli's line.
Named by his dying mother as she hears of the Ark's capture: 'the glory is departed from Israel.'

characters.name: Abinadab of Kirjath-jearim

genealogy.note: NAMING COLLISION, flagged explicitly: this book has three distinct men named Abinadab — this man of Kirjath-jearim (7:1), Jesse's son David's brother (17:13), and Saul's son who dies at Gilboa (31:2).

verses.note: The men of Beth-shemesh send to Kirjath-jearim after the plague-stricken Ark returns; the men there fetch it into 'the house of Abinadab in the hill.'
Sanctifies his son Eleazar to keep the Ark; it remains twenty years while Israel laments after the LORD.

funFacts: The Ark's captivity-and-return arc directly continues the Eli-family judgment thread — it is the object Hophni and Phinehas died escorting into battle.

characters.name: Eleazar son of Abinadab
characters.perkNote: Sanctified specifically to keep the Ark through its twenty years at his father's house — an ongoing personal charge.

verses.note: Sanctified by the men of Kirjath-jearim to keep the Ark of the LORD at his father's house.

characters.name: The Manner of the King
characters.purpose: Warns Israel of the real material cost of trading judges for a king before Saul is confirmed — sons taken for chariots and horsemen, daughters for cooks and bakers, the best fields and a tenth of seed and flocks taken for the king's court — then, once Saul reigns, calls Israel back to covenant obedience rather than treating monarchy as a substitute for faithfulness to the LORD.

verses.note: Israel's elders demand a king 'like all the nations'; Samuel prays, displeased; the LORD tells him the people have not rejected Samuel, 'but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.'
Samuel relays 'the manner of the king' — what a king will take from the people — ending with a warning that they will cry out because of the king they chose and the LORD will not answer that day.

At Gilgal, Samuel calls thunder in wheat harvest as a sign of the people's sin in asking for a king, then reassures them the LORD 'will not forsake his people for his great name's sake,' and vows to keep praying for and teaching them.

characters.name: Samuel

verses.note: As a boy ministering before Eli, hears the LORD call his name three times before Eli recognizes it and teaches him to answer, 'Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth.'
Gathers Israel at Mizpeh, offers a sucking lamb as a whole burnt offering, and cries to the LORD; thunder from heaven routs the attacking Philistines.
Privately anoints Saul with a vial of oil at the LORD's direction, telling him the LORD has anointed him captain over Israel.
Confronts Saul over the spared Amalekite spoil: 'to obey is better than sacrifice'; declares the LORD has rejected him from being king.
Sent to Jesse of Bethlehem; anoints David among his brothers, after which 'the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward.'
David flees to him at Ramah/Naioth; Saul's messengers, then Saul himself, fall to prophesying near Samuel's company.
Dies; all Israel laments him and buries him in his house at Ramah.
Appears (via the woman at Endor) after death, rebukes Saul, and foretells his and his sons' deaths on the morrow.

funFacts: Samuel is the last judge (7:15) and anoints both of Israel's first two kings, making him the hinge figure between the judges era and the monarchy.

characters.name: Saul

genealogy.note: NAMING COLLISION: this Ahinoam (Saul's wife) differs from Ahinoam the Jezreelitess who later marries David (25:43). Separately, 14:49 lists sons Jonathan/Ishui/Melchi-shua while 31:2 at his death lists Jonathan/Abinadab/Malchi-shua — the text never states Ishui and Abinadab are the same person; left as an open question, not resolved.

verses.note: Introduced as Kish's son, 'a choice young man, and a goodly,' taller than any of the people.
Anointed privately by Samuel, then chosen by lot at Mizpeh; found hiding among the baggage; presented to the shouting people.
Delivers Jabesh-gilead from Nahash the Ammonite's siege, his first decisive act as king.
Offers a burnt offering himself unlawfully at Gilgal when Samuel delays; Samuel pronounces his kingdom 'shall not continue.'
Spares Agag and the best spoil against the command to destroy Amalek utterly, leading to his rejection as king.
An evil spirit troubles him; he casts his javelin at David twice while David plays the harp.
Twice spared by David (En-gedi cave; Hachilah camp) and twice acknowledges his own wrong and David's restraint.
Consults the woman with a familiar spirit at Endor after the LORD does not answer by dream, Urim, or prophet; hears Samuel foretell his death.
Mortally wounded by Philistine archers at Gilboa; falls on his own sword after his armourbearer refuses to kill him.

funFacts: 1 Samuel 13:1's reign-length numeral reads incomplete in this translation too ('reigned one year... reigned two years'), matching the recognized textual crux — no reliable age/length is asserted here.

characters.name: Kish
characters.perkNote: His lost asses (9:3) send Saul out searching and put him directly in Samuel's path — the errand that triggers the whole kingship narrative.

verses.note: A Benjamite 'mighty man of power' whose lost asses send Saul searching, leading him to Samuel.

characters.name: Agag
characters.perkNote: Saul's personal decision to spare him, against explicit command, is the specific act for which Saul is rejected as king.

verses.note: Taken alive by Saul, spared along with the best sheep and oxen, against the command to destroy Amalek utterly.
Comes before Samuel 'delicately,' saying 'the bitterness of death is past'; Samuel hews him in pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.

characters.name: Nahash the Ammonite
characters.perkNote: His siege and ultimatum against Jabesh-gilead provoke Saul's first decisive royal act.

verses.note: Besieges Jabesh-gilead, offering terms only on condition of thrusting out every man's right eye, 'a reproach upon all Israel.'

characters.name: The Woman with a Familiar Spirit at Endor
characters.perkNote: Initially refuses out of fear of Saul's own edict against mediums, conducts the seance once sworn an oath, then personally prepares food for the collapsed king.

verses.note: Sought out by a disguised Saul; fears entrapment under his own edict, agrees once sworn an oath, and brings up 'Samuel' at his request.
Sees Saul terrified and weak; urges him to eat and personally prepares a fatted calf and unleavened bread for him and his servants.

characters.name: Abner son of Ner
characters.perkNote: Saul's captain of the host and kinsman; publicly rebuked by David for failing to guard the sleeping king (26:14-16).

genealogy.note: The text names him 'the son of Ner, Saul's uncle' at 14:50; kept as the book's own wording rather than resolving the exact cousin/uncle relationship further.

verses.note: Named as captain of Saul's host.
Asked by Saul whose son the young David is, before bringing David before the king.
Found asleep with the camp under a LORD-sent deep sleep while David and Abishai infiltrate; rebuked by name from a distance for not guarding the king.

characters.name: Saul's Armourbearer
characters.perkNote: Refuses to kill his king even to spare him Philistine mockery, then falls on his own sword to die alongside him once Saul is dead.

verses.note: Asked by the mortally wounded Saul to kill him rather than let the Philistines abuse him; refuses out of fear; after Saul falls on his sword, does likewise and dies with him.

genealogy.mother: Ahinoam, daughter of Ahimaaz (14:50, by inference as Saul's listed wife)

verses.note: With only his armourbearer, climbs to a Philistine garrison at Michmash, convinced 'there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few'; the two kill about twenty men and trigger a rout.
Unknowingly breaks his father's rash oath by eating honey; the people rescue him from Saul's death sentence.
His soul is 'knit with the soul of David'; makes a covenant with him and gives him his robe, garments, sword, bow, and girdle.
Devises the arrow-signal plan to warn David of Saul's intent; the two renew their covenant and part in tears.
Comes to David in the wilderness of Ziph and 'strengthened his hand in God,' telling him he will be king and Jonathan next unto him.
Slain by the Philistines at Mount Gilboa alongside his father.

characters.name: Jonathan's Armourbearer
characters.perkNote: Follows Jonathan into a two-man assault on a Philistine garrison without hesitation: 'behold, I am with thee according to thy heart.'

verses.note: Accompanies Jonathan up to the garrison, pledges full support, and fights alongside him in the attack that kills about twenty men.
Champion of the Philistines of Gath, six cubits and a span tall, with armor and a spear described in detail; defies the armies of Israel.
Presents himself for combat morning and evening for forty days.
Disdains David when he sees him, cursing him by his gods.
Struck in the forehead by David's sling stone, falls, and is killed and beheaded with his own sword.

genealogy.note: NAMING COLLISION: this Ahinoam (David's wife) differs from Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz, Saul's wife (14:50). No children of David appear within this book's own timeframe.

verses.note: The youngest of Jesse's sons, keeping sheep; anointed by Samuel; 'the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward.'
Refuses Saul's armor, takes his sling and five smooth stones, kills Goliath, and beheads him with the giant's own sword.
The women's victory song ('Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands') marks the start of Saul's jealousy.
Flees alone to Ahimelech at Nob, receives hallowed bread and Goliath's sword.
Gathers about four hundred distressed, indebted, or discontented men at the cave of Adullam and becomes their captain.
Secretly cuts off the skirt of Saul's robe in the En-gedi cave rather than kill him, then his heart smites him even for that.
Accepts Abigail's intervention and calls off his planned vengeance on Nabal's household.
Given Ziklag by Achish king of Gath; dwells in Philistine territory over a year.
Sent back from the Philistine muster at Aphek after the lords distrust him, despite Achish's personal defense.

Recovers Ziklag's captives, including his wives, from Amalekite raiders after inquiring of the LORD through Abiathar's ephod; makes it a statute that those guarding the supplies share equally with those who fought.

characters.name: Jesse
characters.perkNote: Presents seven sons before Samuel first, then sends for David from the sheep only once Samuel insists; later sends David with provisions to his brothers at the battle line.

verses.note: Presents seven sons before Samuel, none chosen, until David is sent for from keeping the sheep.
Sends David with bread, cheeses, and parched corn to his brothers serving under Saul against the Philistines.

characters.name: Eliab
characters.perkNote: Jesse's firstborn, passed over by Samuel despite his height (16:6-7); later personally rebukes David's motives at the battle line.

verses.note: Considered for his stature, but rejected: 'the LORD looketh on the heart.'
Angry with David at the battle line, accusing him of pride and coming only to watch the fighting.

characters.name: Achish, King of Gath
characters.perkNote: Grants David Ziklag and personally defends him to suspicious Philistine lords at Aphek before being overruled.

verses.note: David flees to him at Gath and feigns madness; Achish dismisses him as a madman rather than a threat.
Grants David the town of Ziklag rather than housing him in the royal city.
Personally vouches for David before the other Philistine lords but is overruled and must send him back before the battle at Gilboa.

characters.name: Abishai son of Zeruiah
characters.perkNote: Accompanies David alone into Saul's sleeping camp and asks to kill the king with his own spear; restrained by David.

genealogy.note: Identified as brother to Joab (26:6); their father is not named in this book.

verses.note: Volunteers to go with David into Saul's camp; asks to smite the sleeping Saul with his own spear.
Restrained by David; the two take the spear and water-cruse from beside Saul's head instead.

characters.name: The Young Egyptian
characters.perkNote: Found sick and abandoned by his Amalekite master, guides David to the raiding party once fed and sworn a protective oath — a minor figure whose cooperation is the direct cause of David's full recovery of everything taken.

verses.note: Found after three days without food or water, abandoned sick by his Amalekite master; once fed and sworn an oath, agrees to lead David to the raiders.

spouses: Phalti the son of Laish of Gallim, given to her by Saul while David was in exile, 25:44

verses.note: Loves David; given to him as wife after he pays the bride-price of one hundred Philistine foreskins.
Warns David that Saul's messengers watch to kill him and lets him down through a window to escape, placing an image with goats' hair in the bed to deceive them.
Tells Saul David threatened to kill her if she did not help him — her own account to her father.
While David is in exile, Saul gives her instead to Phalti the son of Laish.

genealogy.note: 22:9 and 22:20 both call him 'the son of Ahitub'; 14:3 separately identifies an Ahitub as 'the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli' — combining these makes Ahimelech Eli's great-grandson. NAMING COLLISION: a completely different man, Ahimelech the Hittite (26:6), is one of David's companions and has no other role.

verses.note: Gives fleeing David hallowed shewbread since no ordinary bread is on hand and the young men had kept from women.
Gives David Goliath's sword, kept wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod.
Defends himself and David before Saul, protesting ignorance of any conspiracy.

Condemned by Saul with his whole father's house; Saul's own footmen refuse to strike the LORD's priests, so Doeg the Edomite kills Ahimelech and eighty-five priests personally, then puts Nob itself to the sword.

characters.name: Doeg the Edomite
characters.perkNote: Reports David's visit to Nob, then personally carries out the massacre of eighty-five priests and the town when Saul's own footmen refuse.

genealogy.note: Identified as 'the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul,' 21:7.

verses.note: Present at Nob 'detained before the LORD' when David comes to Ahimelech; witnesses the exchange.
Reports to Saul that Ahimelech gave David bread, Goliath's sword, and inquired of the LORD for him.
Personally slays eighty-five priests when Saul's servants refuse, then puts Nob to the sword, men, women, children, and livestock.
The one son of Ahimelech to escape the massacre at Nob; flees to David, who tells him, 'abide thou with me, fear not... with me thou shalt be in safeguard.'
Brings an ephod down to David at Keilah; David uses it to inquire of the LORD.
Brings David the ephod again at Ziklag; David inquires of the LORD before pursuing the Amalekite raiders.
Introduced as 'a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance,' wife of the 'churlish and evil' Nabal.
Warned by a servant of Nabal's insult; quickly gathers bread, wine, dressed sheep, parched corn, raisins, and fig cakes and rides to meet David without telling her husband.
Intercedes before David, takes the blame on herself, and persuades him not to shed blood, prophesying the LORD will make him 'a sure house.'
David blesses her discretion, accepts her gift, and calls off his planned attack.
Once Nabal has died, agrees to become David's wife: 'let thine handmaid be a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.'
Taken captive with Ahinoam when the Amalekites raid Ziklag; recovered by David along with all other captives.

characters.name: Nabal
characters.perkNote: His insulting refusal to provision David's men is the entire inciting cause of the chapter-25 conflict that Abigail's wisdom then resolves.

genealogy.note: 'Of the house of Caleb' (25:3); the text plays directly on his name meaning 'fool' (25:25).

verses.note: A wealthy sheep-owner of Maon with property in Carmel, described as 'churlish and evil in his doings.'
Refuses David's request for provisions with contempt: 'Who is David?... shall I then take my bread, and my water... and give it unto men, whom I know not whence they be?'

Holds a drunken feast 'like the feast of a king'; on hearing what Abigail did the next morning, 'his heart died within him, and he became as a stone'; about ten days later, the LORD smites him and he dies.
Offered to David by Saul as a wife on condition of fighting the LORD's battles (a pretext exposing David to danger); given instead to Adriel the Meholathite.

eighty_five_priests_of_nob.note: Records eighty-five men 'that did wear a linen ephod' slain by Doeg at Saul's command, along with the rest of Nob (22:19). None individually named.

samuels_sons.note: Names Samuel's sons Joel and Abiah, made judges in Beersheba; their bribe-taking and perverted judgment is described collectively, not differentiated between the two.

jesses_other_sons.note: Jesse had eight sons total. Beyond David, only Eliab is individually differentiated (he rebukes David at the battle line, 17:28). Abinadab and Shammah are named only as present with Saul's army, with no distinguishing action. Four more sons are entirely unnamed.

sauls_other_children.note: 14:49 lists sons Jonathan, Ishui, and Melchi-shua; 31:2 at his death lists Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua. The text does not itself state Ishui and Abinadab are the same person — treated as an open question. Merab and Michal are Saul's two named daughters (14:49).

men_of_jabesh_gilead.note: The men of Jabesh-gilead who recover and bury Saul's and his sons' bodies by night after Beth-shan are unnamed collectively — a bookend to Saul's earlier deliverance of that same city in chapter 11.

ahimelech_the_hittite.note: One of two men David asks to accompany him into Saul's camp; only Abishai is shown going (26:7). Unrelated to Ahimelech priest of Nob — flagged as a same-book naming collision.

naming_collisions_master_list.note: (1) Abinadab — three distinct men: of Kirjath-jearim (7:1), Jesse's son (17:13), Saul's son (31:2). (2) Ahinoam — two distinct women: Saul's wife (14:50) and Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, David's wife (25:43). (3) Ahimelech — priest of Nob (21-22) versus Ahimelech the Hittite (26:6). (4) Phinehas — Eli's son (this book) versus Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron, a different book/person entirely. (5) Ahitub — the Ahitub of 14:3/22:9,20 (this book's priestly line) versus a later, different Ahitub outside this book. (6) Abigail — David's wife here versus a different, later Abigail outside this book. (7) Jonathan — a common name reused elsewhere in scripture; within 1 Samuel it refers only to Saul's son.
